limitations: A patch test is a consistency (necessary) condition; it proves constant-curvature reproduction, not coarse-mesh accuracy or pointwise moment accuracy.
The distorted-patch residual is an interpolation limitation of the bilinear w field (quadratic exact field), measured and h-convergent, not a defect.
A Dirichlet-driven patch contains no zero-energy mode, so this test cannot detect the rank deficiency of the one-point (sri) element.

The free-edge strip leg of the Poisson cross-check is NOT converged at n_y=2: its converged offset is ~1.2% (L/b=5) and it decays with L/b, i.e. it is a clamped-root end effect, not a discretization error. The leg is therefore graded only after transverse convergence, and the coupling itself is graded on the exact M_y=0 state.

The closed-form Poisson ratio is an algebra identity (insensitive to the element); it is reported as an oracle check, not as element evidence. Round 1 graded it as if it were the cross-check -- that gate could not fail.

Literature criterion cited from the standard statement; the textbooks were not retrievable offline, but every target value is evaluated in code from the closed form, so no table digit enters the evidence chain.
